mustFix.title: Decision 6 states a rule about D-056 gate 1 that D-056's text does not contain and that the adopted DR-102 Class A recording falsifies
mustFix.finding: Decision 6 reads: 'The v3 contract remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING, so Eligibility gate 1 does not hold. Not eligible in kind. Not SATISFIED.' Gate 1 Class A, in the pinned D-056 turn-2 subject, is: 'An independently accepted design contract exists at 0 blockers with application-grade acceptance and no express reservation (D-001 T2-02), recorded by a D-000 entry; the row's lead label is `OPEN`.' It tests acceptance properties, a D-000 recording, and the row's lead label. It says nothing about applied-state or binding force. The precedent settles it against the entry. D-085 records DR-102 SATISFIED under D-056 Class A, and DR-102's design contract is control-protocol-contract.v2, whose own fields read status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL. If being CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED barred Class A, D-085 was unlawful — and no design contract in this corpus could ever support Class A, because every one of them is recorded as a candidate that binds nothing. That is the doctrine this sentence would put on the record. The timing makes it worse rather than better: this is the act that, by its own Decisions 5 and 6, leaves all seven DR-133 remainders as execution named at DR-G* obligations with owners, so the first question the next cycle asks is which eligibility gate still fails. It would get the answer 'gate 1, because the contract is a candidate', which is wrong, and which a later reviewer could equally turn around into an attack on D-085.
mustFix.whyMustFix: The conclusion is conservative and probably right, but a stated rule that the cited instrument contradicts has been blocker-grade throughout this corpus, and this one contradicts both D-056's own gate text and an adopted decision that relied on the opposite reading. Recording it would leave two adopted entries in direct conflict about what Class A requires.
mustFix.repair: Keep the conclusion and replace the reason. Two correct grounds are available, and either suffices. First, gate 1's remaining limb — application-grade acceptance with no express reservation — is not established here: the Claude 2 v3 verdict grades the acceptance as 'ACCEPT as an independently reviewed DR-133 design-contract candidate' and states in terms that it 'does not apply the artifact, does not mark DR-133 SATISFIED, and does not open D-056 Class A'. Second, gate 4 reserves the eligibility determination to a later dedicated D-000 cycle with independent SATISFIED-GRADE review, which this entry is not and does not claim to be. While correcting it, say plainly what Decisions 5 and 6 currently imply only by arithmetic — that after this act gates 2 and 3 hold for all seven classes — so the later cycle can see exactly which gate remains and on what ground.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 1 MUST-FIX. Thirteen attacks run, one landed. Custody is clean and the MF-6 was not applied: 2bfe6d92 at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left 94250a8, file 08 byte-identical at both ends with its gate table still ending at DR-G22, COORD at its pin, and all six file pins plus the D-146 commit pin reproducing. The mechanics are the most careful work in this sequence. The condition-4 cell quoted for replacement is byte-exact against live file 08. The new row carries eight fields in the live header's order, with a harness cell built like G20's and G21's. Every count reconciles against the table I counted myself: 22 gate rows today at 19 OPEN and 3 HARD-BLOCKED, so 20 OPEN and 3 HARD-BLOCKED after the insert; owners 22 of 22 to 23 of 23; required gates 18 of 18 to 19 of 19 with D-147 added to the attribution list. The insertion anchor is unambiguous, since the DR-G22 row really is followed by one blank line and the Blueprint-readiness heading. The 65-row preamble is correctly left alone: I counted 87 DR- rows, 22 of them gates, so the figure excludes gates exactly. D-018 item 2 confirms gates are one of the six D-002 sets and that changes take a scoped successor with its own review, which is what Limb A is. And my advisory about the nineteenth row is answered structurally rather than cited — the identifier is named in the same act, so condition 4 holds at 19 of 19. What blocks is one sentence of doctrine. Decision 6 says the v3 contract remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING, so Eligibility gate 1 does not hold. D-056 gate 1 Class A tests an independently accepted contract at 0 blockers with application-grade acceptance and no express reservation, recorded by a D-000 entry, with the row's lead label OPEN. It says nothing about applied-state. And the precedent falsifies the reason outright: D-085 recorded DR-102 SATISFIED under Class A on control-protocol-contract.v2, whose own fields read CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, DO-NOT-SEAL. If that state barred Class A, D-085 was unlawful and no design contract in this corpus could ever support Class A. The conclusion — not eligible in kind, not SATISFIED — is very likely right, and two correct grounds are available: gate 1's application-grade limb is not established here, since my own v3 verdict grades the acceptance as candidate-grade and says in terms that it does not open Class A; and gate 4 reserves the determination to a later dedicated SATISFIED-GRADE cycle. Correcting the reason costs a sentence, and while correcting it the entry should say plainly what Decisions 5 and 6 now imply only by arithmetic — that gates 2 and 3 hold for all seven classes after this act — so the next cycle sees exactly which gate remains and why.
